goals: Close verified masonry material-form holes with locally derived, reference-faithful additive blocks for the owner's private modpack.
Keep Interchangeable Block Families as the sole Clutter No More ShapeMap authority while AMC owns only its original blocks, data, recipes, and presentation.
scope: Canary 5 retains the approved 646-cell masonry audit across 17 profiles: 409 existing Minecraft/BBB/Macaw cells remain provider-owned and AMC registers only the 237 genuine gaps, including native controls, BBB details, Macaw paths/pavings/patterns, and Macaw Windows forms.

C5 semantically resolves model references separately from concrete texture sprites, including inherited texture variables; protected provider-derived closures and the JAR remain generated only into ignored local paths.
C5 remains an additive content candidate: it supplies no ShapeMap data, no provider-registry inference, no compatibility implementation, and no claimed manual Minecraft runtime result.

exclusions: Committing, pushing, publishing, or redistributing provider-derived models, textures, blockstates, recipes, data, or derivative JAR bytes. Exact local private derivation from BBB and Macaw reference artifacts is owner-authorized only through ignored build and artifact paths.
A second ShapeMap, equivalence, switching, recipe-cleanup, networking, or storage system; Interchangeable Block Families remains the sole authority for those concerns.
Dynamic material discovery, registry-name or tag inference, provider mutation, replacing a provider block, or creating an alternate item in another provider namespace.
Minecraft deployment, testing-profile access, runtime-state mutation, acceptance, or inferring manual runtime success from static checks.
